cards.title: THE GUEST BATHROOM
cards.tagline: FIVE ZONES. START WITH THE COUNTER THE VISITOR SEES FIRST.
cards.objective: The guest bathroom is the one room a visitor spends time in alone, with the door shut and nothing to look at but your standards. This card is the map and the order.
cards.start_here: GHZ-001 Guest Vanity Counter. Do the vanity counter first and the linen shelf last. The counter takes one trip and changes how the whole room reads; the linen shelf needs a wash cycle to finish, so put the stored towels in the machine before you touch anything else and let them run while you work the rest of the room.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your bathroom. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do GHA-011 The Full Guest Bathroom Hazard Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers the cord beside the basin, the chemicals under the cabinet, the tub floor, and the water heater in the linen closet.

cards.title: GUEST VANITY COUNTER
cards.tagline: THREE THINGS LIVE HERE: SOAP, TISSUES, A TOWEL. NOTHING ELSE.
cards.objective: It gives a visitor somewhere to wash their hands and set a phone down, with nothing of yours in the way.
callouts: A soap pump standing above half full on the counter
One folded hand towel hanging on a ring visible from the doorway
A box of tissues sitting at the back corner clear of splash
A clear stretch of bare counter wide enough for a phone and a pair of glasses
No toothbrush cup or hair clips anywhere on the counter
A dry, ring-free patch of counter under the soap dispenser
cards.done_looks_like: A soap pump above half full, one folded hand towel on the ring where you can see it from the doorway, a box of tissues at the back corner, and enough bare counter to set down a phone and a pair of glasses. No toothbrush cup holding your family's toothbrushes, no hair clips behind the tap, no dried soap ring under the dispenser.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: Anything with a cord left plugged in next to a basin that a guest will fill. Unplug and store after every use, and keep the cord off the counter entirely.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Glass tumblers and glass decorative dishes on a wet counter. When one goes over in a small tiled room, someone is standing there barefoot.

the_call.title: Whose bathroom is this really
the_call.text: If a child or a housemate genuinely brushes their teeth in here, the hotel counter standard loses every time and you end up resetting it twice a week. The decision you have been dodging is which room this actually is. Pick out loud: either it is a used bathroom, in which case one named person gets a labeled caddy or drawer and the counter holds their two items alongside the guest three, or it is a guest bathroom, in which case that toothbrush moves today and nothing personal comes back. Holding a hotel standard against a resident who lives here is not a discipline problem, it is a standard aimed at the wrong room.

supplies: Streak-free glass and mirror cleaner (not in this zone's list, and the mirror needs it)

cards.title: GUEST VANITY STORAGE
cards.tagline: TWO BINS. ONE LABELED GUEST, ONE LABELED CLEANING. THE BASE STAYS BARE.
cards.objective: It holds the things a guest might otherwise have to ask you for, plus the cleaning kit that keeps this room ready.
callouts: A bin labeled Guest Supplies holding a new toothbrush and a wrapped bar of soap
A small dish holding four unopened travel toiletries inside that same bin
A bin labeled Cleaning holding bowl cleaner, glass spray and cloths standing upright
Four rolls of toilet paper stacked in plain view
A bare cabinet base with nothing loose sitting on it
Both bins standing light enough to lift out with one hand
cards.done_looks_like: Open the door and see two lift-out bins and nothing loose: one labeled for guest supplies holding a new toothbrush, a wrapped bar of soap, and four unopened travel toiletries in a small dish, and one labeled for cleaning holding bowl cleaner, glass spray, and cloths standing upright on a shallow tray. Four rolls of toilet paper stacked in plain view. The cabinet base is bare enough that a single drip from the trap would show.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Bowl cleaner, bleach, and drain opener stored under the sink of the bathroom where a visiting child gets sent alone. Latch the door or move the chemicals out of the room.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A slow weep from the trap that nobody sees because nobody opens this cabinet. It reaches the tile as a thin invisible film long before it shows as a puddle.

the_call.title: The bag of hotel miniatures
the_call.text: The collection of tiny shampoos is the hardest thing in this cabinet, because throwing out free soap feels like waste and keeping it feels like hospitality, so it has sat there for years doing neither. Settle it with arithmetic: a guest staying two nights uses one shampoo, one conditioner, one soap, and one lotion. So keep four, unopened, the four with the least battered labels, and put them in a small dish where they read as an offering rather than a hoard. The rest go today. If binning them is genuinely beyond you, they go into a shelter donation box this week, in the car, not back on the shelf.

supplies: Neutral pH multi-surface cleaner (not in this zone's list, but the sealed cabinet interior needs it)
Color-coded microfiber cloth set (not in this zone's list, and you cannot wipe the cabinet down without cloths)

cards.title: SHOWER OR TUB
cards.tagline: THREE BOTTLES. ONE MAT. ONE THING BOLTED IN TO GRAB.
cards.objective: It has to be ready for someone to shower in tonight, even though nobody has used it since spring.
callouts: Three bottles in a hanging caddy, shampoo, conditioner and body wash, each more than a third full
A curtain liner or glass screen with no pink film along its bottom edge
A bath mat folded over the tub rim rather than lying wet on the floor
Grout the same even color in the corners as in the middle
A non-slip surface visible on the tub floor
One securely anchored grab point fixed to the wall, not a towel bar
cards.done_looks_like: Three bottles in the caddy, all recognizable and more than a third full, a curtain liner or glass screen with no pink film along the bottom edge, a bath mat folded over the tub rim rather than lying wet on the floor, and grout that is the same color in the corners as it is in the middle. A non-slip surface underfoot inside the tub.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: An unfamiliar tub with a slick glazed floor, used at night by someone who does not know the room. A non-slip mat or strips are the fix, not a warning.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A towel bar or a suction rail being used as a grab handle. Both let go under load, and the person comes down against the tub rim on the way.

the_call.title: The grout you cannot clean
the_call.text: You have scrubbed one grout line three times, it stayed gray, and you have quietly started calling that clean. It is not dirt. It is mold that has grown into porous grout or a silicone bead that has failed underneath, and no product will bring it back, so every week you spend part of the clean on a job that cannot succeed. The rule: give a stained line one proper treatment with full dwell time and a stiff brush. If it darkens again within two weeks, stop cleaning it and move it to the repair list, which means raking out and regrouting, or cutting out the old silicone and running a fresh bead. Calling it a repair is the decision. It is a Saturday afternoon once, instead of a chore forever.

supplies: Dedicated mildew remover (not in this zone's list, for grout the soap-film cleaner will not shift)
Stiff grout or detail brush (not in this zone's list, and the grout and the non-slip floor need bristles)

cards.title: TOILET AREA
cards.tagline: ONE ROLL IN SIGHT. A DRY BRUSH. A LINER IN THE CAN.
cards.objective: It has to be clean and stocked in a way that is obvious to someone who will never ask you where anything is.
callouts: One spare toilet roll standing in a holder within reach of a seated person
A dry toilet brush resting in its holder with no liquid pooled in the bottom
A small trash can with a liner actually fitted inside it
No ring visible at the bowl's water line
A dry, dust-free floor behind the pedestal
A bare tank top with nothing standing on it
cards.done_looks_like: One spare roll standing in plain sight on the tank or in a holder a seated person can reach without standing up. A brush that is dry, resting in a holder with no liquid pooled in the bottom. A small trash can with a liner actually in it. No ring at the water line, and a dry, dust-free floor behind the pedestal.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Bleach and an acid bowl or limescale cleaner used one after the other in a small room with the door closed and no fan running. Use one product, ventilate, and never store the two together.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: A bowl cleaner bottle left standing behind the pedestal after cleaning. It is at floor level, in reach, and the cap is rarely back on properly.

the_call.title: The brush nobody wants to touch
the_call.text: The toilet brush in a guest bathroom is the object your household has silently agreed not to look at. It has splayed bristles, it stands in an inch of gray water in the bottom of its holder, and it has been there for years, spreading more than it removes. The decision you are avoiding is that a brush is a consumable, not a fixture. The rule: splayed bristles or liquid in the holder means both go out today and a fresh set comes in, and from then on the brush gets rinsed in the flush and left propped under the closed seat to drip before it goes back in the holder. If that much handling is more than you will realistically do, buy the kind with a disposable head and stop negotiating with yourself about it.

supplies: Toilet bowl cleaner and a dedicated bowl brush (not in this zone's list, and the bowl needs both)

cards.title: GUEST LINEN ZONE
cards.tagline: TWO BUNDLES. ONE LIFT EACH. THE MAT UNDERNEATH.
cards.objective: It holds one complete fresh set of towels so hosting never starts with a search.
callouts: Two complete towel bundles, each holding a bath towel, hand towel and washcloth folded together
Both bundles matching in color with neither carrying a musty smell
A clean bath mat folded flat beneath the bundles
A hand's width of clear air above the stack
No thin gray towel or dog towel sharing the shelf
A hand's width of clearance kept around anything on the shelf that runs hot
cards.done_looks_like: One bundle per expected guest, each holding a bath towel, a hand towel, and a washcloth folded together, matching in color, smelling of nothing at all. A clean bath mat folded flat beneath the bundles. A hand's width of air above the stack. No thin gray towel kept for the dog sharing the shelf.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: Textiles stacked against a water heater, a hot pipe, or its power cable in a shared closet. Keep a hand's width of clear air on every hot side.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A bath mat with a curled or hardened rubber backing. It stops gripping the tile and slides out from under someone stepping off wet.

the_call.title: The good towels
the_call.text: Every house has a set of nice towels that guests are not quite allowed to use and a set of worn ones that guests actually get, and nobody ever says this out loud. Towels thin whether they are used or not, so holding the good ones back means they will age untouched in a closet while your visitors dry off on something gray. The rule: the guest bundle is built from the best towels you own, put into service today, and the ones they replace get demoted to rags on the same trip so they cannot creep back. And if a towel is genuinely too good for a guest to use, then it is not linen, it is a keepsake, and it belongs anywhere except the towel shelf.

supplies: Washing machine (not a listed product, but the stored linens need a hot wash)

cards.title: THE GOOD TOWELS ARE STILL FOLDED IN THE CLOSET
cards.tagline: WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. THEN WHY.
cards.objective: The best towels in the house are still folded in the closet years later, while guests dry off on ones that have gone thin and gray.

branches.answer: Using the nice ones feels like using them up, so they get held back instead
Nobody's decided the worn ones should actually retire, so they just keep getting reissued
A towel that just sits folded doesn't look like it needs a decision, thin fold line and all

cards.title: A BUNDLE LEFT THIS SHELF MIDWEEK AND NEVER CAME BACK
cards.tagline: WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. THEN WHY.
cards.objective: A bundle taken from this shelf midweek for some other use is never the one that comes back.

branches.answer: Nothing here tracks what left, so the gap is only found by the next guest
There's no single person who restocks this shelf after it's been raided
Taking a towel from here doesn't trigger anything that says to replace it

cards.title: ONE GUEST SET MEANS THREE SEPARATE STOPS
cards.tagline: WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. THEN WHY.
cards.objective: Making up a guest set means grabbing a bath towel from one stack, a hand towel from a shelf across the closet, and a washcloth that matches neither.

branches.answer: Towels are stored by type instead of as ready sets, so what should be one lift turns into three separate stops
Nobody decided guest towels should be pre-bundled, so they default to being grouped by size instead
It's always been sorted this way, so the extra hunting doesn't register as a real problem

cards.objective: More things are kept here than the zone's job needs.

cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Look for the four: a blade your hand would meet, weight above shoulder height, heat beside something that burns, and an unsafe placement near a child's reach.

cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Find the last one of something you use daily. If nothing tells you it is the last one, you will find out at the worst possible moment.

cards.objective: Two people run one zone by two designs, so it is permanently half of each.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Do the shared task together, once. The argument that starts is the conflict, and it is a design problem, not a character problem.

cards.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
cards.objective: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask who resets this zone. If the honest answer is "whoever gets to it" or two names with no agreement, there is no owner.

cards.title: SENTIMENTAL ATTACHMENT
cards.objective: The item is kept for what it represents, not because it is used, and the guilt stalls Sort indefinitely.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask if you would buy this again today for what it does. If the answer is no but you still cannot decide, the hold is sentimental.

cards.title: UNRESOLVED DECISION
cards.objective: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Pick up one piece. If your first thought is a verb (pay, sign, call, decide) rather than a place, it needs a decision, not a home.

cards.objective: Reaching the surface to clean it costs more effort than the rest of the zone combined, so it gets skipped.

cards.title: PERCEPTUAL BLINDNESS
cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: CLEAR THE COUNTER TO THREE THINGS
cards.objective: Take everything off the counter and put back only what a visitor would use, so nothing of the household's is left in view.
cards.why_it_matters: A counter holding a housemate's toothbrush or a stray hair clip stops reading as a guest counter and starts reading as an argument about whose bathroom this is.
inputs: a small box for anything going back to another room
steps: Take everything off the counter and put back only what a visitor would use: soap, tissues, hand towel. The travel conditioner, the spare contact lens case, and the razor that ended up here because the main bathroom ran out of room all go back where they belong or into the trash.
Set the soap, tissues and towel back in their usual spots, clear of the basin.
cards.victory_condition: Only soap, tissues and a folded hand towel remain on the counter, with bare space enough for a phone and glasses, and nothing of the household's left behind.

art.subject: a bathroom vanity counter mid-clear, a small box of personal items being carried out and only soap, tissues and a folded towel remaining
must_show: Only soap, tissues and a folded hand towel remain on the counter, with bare space enough for a phone and glasses, and nothing of the household's left behind.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SETTLE WHOSE BATHROOM THIS IS AND PHOTOGRAPH THE STANDARD
cards.objective: Decide out loud whether this is a used bathroom or a guest bathroom, then photograph the three-item counter and post the picture inside the vanity door.
cards.why_it_matters: Holding a hotel standard against a resident who genuinely uses this room is aimed at the wrong room, and it gets reset twice a week until somebody decides.
steps: Ask out loud whether anyone in the house actually uses this bathroom day to day.
If yes, give that person one named drawer or caddy for their two items, alongside the guest three; if no, agree that nothing personal comes back to this counter, starting today.
Photograph the counter holding exactly its agreed items and tape the picture inside the vanity door.
cards.victory_condition: One decision is made and photographed: either a named resident has their own labeled spot, or nothing personal returns to this counter.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand taping a photograph of a settled bathroom counter to the inside of a vanity cabinet door
must_show: One decision is made and photographed: either a named resident has their own labeled spot, or nothing personal returns to this counter.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE MINIATURES AND SEND BACKSTOCK HOME
cards.objective: Pull everything out of the cabinet, be honest about years of hotel miniatures, and return anything that drifted in from another bathroom.
cards.why_it_matters: A miniature kept because throwing out free soap feels wasteful still takes up the same shelf as the four a guest would actually use.
steps: Pull everything out and be honest about the hotel miniatures: the shampoos from three trips, the lotion nobody opened, the free conditioner samples. Keep the unopened ones a guest would actually use, throw out the started ones, and send household backstock that drifted in here back to the bathroom it came from.
Keep four unopened travel toiletries with the least battered labels in a small dish; bag the rest for donation or the bin.
cards.victory_condition: Every started miniature and drifted household item is gone, and only unopened travel toiletries a guest would actually use remain.

art.subject: a hand sorting a pile of hotel miniature bottles into a keep dish of four and a donation bag of the rest
must_show: Every started miniature and drifted household item is gone, and only unopened travel toiletries a guest would actually use remain.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LABEL TWO BINS AND LATCH THE CLEANING SHELF
cards.objective: Set up two labeled lift-out bins, draw a minimum line for toilet paper, and move or latch anything a crawling child could reach.
cards.why_it_matters: Bowl cleaner and bleach sitting under this sink are exactly at a visiting toddler's eye level, and a bare cabinet base is the only way a slow leak from the trap ever gets seen.
steps: Write two labels by hand, Guest Supplies and Cleaning, and load each bin accordingly.
Draw a line on the shelf at the toilet paper minimum, and stack rolls in plain view above it.
Fit the cabinet with a childproof latch or move the cleaning bin to a high shelf elsewhere, and never store bleach beside an acid bowl or limescale cleaner.
cards.victory_condition: Two labeled bins sit on a bare base, toilet paper stands visible above its drawn line, and the cleaning products are latched away from a child's reach.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: two labeled lift-out bins standing in an open vanity cabinet beside a visible stack of toilet paper, a childproof latch fitted to the cabinet door
must_show: Two labeled bins sit on a bare base, toilet paper stands visible above its drawn line, and the cleaning products are latched away from a child's reach.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE REJECTED BOTTLES
cards.objective: Take out every bottle, turn it over, and keep only one shampoo, one conditioner and one body wash, all more than a third full.
cards.why_it_matters: A bottle nobody liked does not improve by staying on the tub floor, it just collects a sticky ring underneath it.
steps: Take out every bottle and turn it over. This is where the household's rejected products retire: the shampoo nobody liked, the body wash that smells wrong, the conditioner welded to the shelf. Keep one shampoo, one conditioner, one body wash, all readable and more than a third full. The rest go, along with the old razor and the disintegrating loofah.
Wipe the sticky ring left on the tub floor or shelf under each bottle removed.
cards.victory_condition: One shampoo, one conditioner and one body wash stand in the shower, each more than a third full and easy to read, with nothing else left welded to the shelf.

art.subject: a hand lifting a welded shampoo bottle off a tub floor, one shampoo, one conditioner and one body wash left standing in a hanging caddy
must_show: One shampoo, one conditioner and one body wash stand in the shower, each more than a third full and easy to read, with nothing else left welded to the shelf.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: TREAT THE GROUT, HANG THE MAT, ANCHOR A GRAB BAR
cards.objective: Give a stained grout line one proper treatment with full dwell time, fit a non-slip mat, and install one solidly anchored grab point.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest steps into an unfamiliar tub at night on a surface they cannot judge, and a towel bar screwed into drywall tears out the moment it takes a person's weight.
inputs: a non-slip mat or adhesive strips
steps: Spray the stained grout line with dedicated mildew remover, leave it for full dwell time, then work it with a stiff grout brush and rinse.
If it darkens again within two weeks, stop cleaning it and move it to the repair list instead.
Fit a non-slip mat or adhesive strips to the tub floor, and install one securely anchored grab bar, never relying on a towel bar.
cards.victory_condition: The treated grout line holds its color for two weeks, a non-slip mat sits on the tub floor, and one solidly anchored grab bar is fixed to the wall.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand pressing a stiff grout brush into a shower corner beside a freshly fitted non-slip mat and a securely anchored wall grab bar
must_show: The treated grout line holds its color for two weeks, a non-slip mat sits on the tub floor, and one solidly anchored grab bar is fixed to the wall.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE TANK TOP AND FLOOR BEHIND THE BOWL
cards.objective: Clear everything from the top of the tank and the floor behind the bowl, leaving one reserve roll standing in the open.
cards.why_it_matters: A pile of air fresheners and old magazines behind the bowl is where a guest bathroom's clutter hides longest, because nobody but a guest ever looks there.
inputs: a box for anything worth keeping elsewhere
steps: Clear everything from the top of the tank and the floor behind the bowl: the collection of air fresheners, the second brush, the magazines, the box of something nobody has identified in years. One reserve roll stays in the open. Nothing else.
Bin anything unidentifiable and rehome anything genuinely useful to where it is actually used.
cards.victory_condition: The tank top and the floor behind the bowl are bare except for one reserve roll standing in the open.

art.subject: a bare toilet tank top and floor behind the bowl with a single reserve roll standing in the open, a bin bag sitting nearby
must_show: The tank top and the floor behind the bowl are bare except for one reserve roll standing in the open.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: MOVE THE ROLL WITHIN SEATED REACH AND RETIRE THE BRUSH
cards.objective: Remount the reserve roll where a seated person can reach it, and replace a splayed or standing-water brush with a fresh one.
cards.why_it_matters: A reserve roll nobody seated can reach defeats the entire point of having one, and a brush that has stood in gray water for years spreads more than it removes.
inputs: a new toilet brush and holder
steps: Remount or reposition the roll holder so a seated person can reach it without standing up.
Replace a brush with splayed bristles or standing water in its holder with a fresh set.
Agree the new routine: rinse the brush in the flush and prop it to drip under the closed seat before it goes back in the holder.
cards.victory_condition: The reserve roll is reachable from a seated position, and a fresh, dry brush stands in a dry holder.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a toilet paper holder remounted within easy seated reach, a fresh dry toilet brush standing in a clean holder beside it
must_show: The reserve roll is reachable from a seated position, and a fresh, dry brush stands in a dry holder.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: RETIRE THE THIN AND GRAY TOWELS
cards.objective: Unfold every towel in daylight and pull anything thin, gray, stiff or stained out of the guest stack for good.
cards.why_it_matters: A towel that looks fine folded in closet light shows its wear the moment it is unfolded in daylight, and a guest is the one who finds out first.
steps: Unfold every towel and look at it in daylight rather than closet light. Anything thin along the fold line, permanently gray, stiff from too much softener, or carrying a hair dye or nosebleed stain comes out of the guest stack. It becomes a rag or a car towel today. It does not go back just in case.
Move the household's best remaining towels into the guest stack to replace what left.
cards.victory_condition: Every towel remaining in the guest stack is free of thinning, graying, stiffness or stains, and none of it went back in just in case.

art.subject: a hand unfolding a thin, graying towel in daylight beside a stack of newly promoted guest towels
must_show: Every towel remaining in the guest stack is free of thinning, graying, stiffness or stains, and none of it went back in just in case.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: BUNDLE BY GUEST, MARK THE LINE, WASH THE STORED SET
cards.objective: Fold towels into complete guest bundles rather than stacks by type, mark the shelf at the second bundle's edge, and wash the stored set even though nobody has used it.
cards.why_it_matters: Gathering a bath towel from one stack and a washcloth from another turns one guest's setup into three separate searches, and a towel that sat folded all season carries a musty note the instant it gets wet.
steps: Fold each bath towel, hand towel and washcloth together into one bundle, so setting up for a guest is one lift.
Mark the shelf edge where the second bundle should end.
Wash the whole stored set and the bath mat on a hot cycle before refolding, even though nobody has used them.
cards.victory_condition: Two complete bundles sit on the shelf up to the marked line, freshly washed, with the bath mat folded beneath them.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: two complete folded towel bundles on a linen shelf beside a marker line showing where the second bundle ends
must_show: Two complete bundles sit on the shelf up to the marked line, freshly washed, with the bath mat folded beneath them.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FULL GUEST BATHROOM HAZARD WALK
cards.objective: Walk every zone checking for a plugged-in cord beside water, a chemical within a child's reach, a slick tub floor, and any textile stacked against the water heater.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest brings an unfamiliar body, sometimes a visiting child, into a room the household almost never uses, so the hazards a daily bathroom would surface get found here only if someone looks on purpose.
steps: Check the counter for any cord plugged in beside the basin and any glass standing on a wet surface, and clear both.
Check under the vanity for bowl cleaner or bleach within a child's reach, and latch the cabinet if it is not already.
Check the tub for a non-slip mat and one securely anchored grab point, and check the linen closet for a hand's width of clearance around the water heater.
cards.victory_condition: No cord sits beside water, no chemical sits within a child's reach, the tub has a non-slip surface and an anchored grab point, and nothing touches the water heater.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand checking a childproof latch on a vanity cabinet in a guest bathroom, a non-slip mat visible in the tub beyond
must_show: No cord sits beside water, no chemical sits within a child's reach, the tub has a non-slip surface and an anchored grab point, and nothing touches the water heater.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE VISIT-CONFIRMED WALK-THROUGH
cards.objective: The moment a visit is confirmed, walk the whole room once: top up the soap, hang a fresh towel, check the reserve roll, and confirm two linen bundles are ready.
cards.why_it_matters: This room has no daily user, so nothing forces a check except someone deciding to do one before a guest arrives.
steps: Top up the soap and hang a fresh hand towel on the counter.
Confirm the reserve roll is upright and a fresh liner is in the trash can.
Confirm two complete towel bundles stand on the linen shelf up to the marked line.
cards.victory_condition: The whole room was checked the moment the visit was confirmed, and one named person did it.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand hanging a fresh folded towel on a guest bathroom counter ring, a full soap pump and a spare toilet roll visible nearby
must_show: The whole room was checked the moment the visit was confirmed, and one named person did it.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE DEPARTURE RESET
cards.objective: The moment a guest leaves, strip the bathroom the same way you strip the bed: run everything they used through one wash, and restock the linen shelf before you sit down.
cards.why_it_matters: A towel taken from this shelf midweek is never the one that comes back unless the departure itself is what triggers the reset.
steps: Carry out whatever the guest left in the shower or on the counter to the laundry on the same trip as the bed sheets.
Wash the used towels and bath mat together in one load.
Refold and restock the linen shelf to two complete bundles before considering the room done.
cards.victory_condition: Everything the guest used is through the wash, and two complete bundles stand ready on the shelf again.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a laundry basket holding used guest towels and a bath mat beside a linen shelf being restocked to two bundles
must_show: Everything the guest used is through the wash, and two complete bundles stand ready on the shelf again.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: GUEST VANITY COUNTER STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: The counter holds three things: soap, tissues, hand towel. Anything a visitor brings leaves with them.
cards.trigger: When you put away fresh towels after laundry, swap the guest hand towel in the same motion.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the collar at the base of the tap where a chalky ring hides, working it with a folded cloth corner until it lifts.
Lift the soap pump and wipe the sticky ring under its base before setting it back down.
Wipe the towel ring and its mount clean before you rehang a fresh folded towel.

art.subject: a bathroom vanity counter holding a soap pump standing above half full, a single folded hand towel hanging on a ring by the door, a box of tissues at the back corner, and a clear stretch of bare counter with no toothbrush cup or hair clips in view, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: GUEST VANITY STORAGE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Two labeled lift-out bins and a visible toilet paper stack. Nothing loose on the cabinet base, so a leak has somewhere obvious to show.
cards.trigger: You already open this cabinet to get the brush for the weekly bowl clean, so run a hand across the base while you are down there.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the neck and cap of one bottle in each bin where dried product has run down the side.
Run a hand across the bare cabinet base, feeling for a dark ring or a soft patch near the trap.
Wipe the inside face of the cabinet door and its handle before closing it.

art.subject: the inside of an open bathroom vanity cabinet holding two labeled lift-out bins, one marked Guest Supplies with a wrapped soap bar and travel toiletries in a small dish, one marked Cleaning with bottles standing upright on a tray, four rolls of toilet paper stacked beside them, and a bare cabinet base, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: SHOWER OR TUB STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: One shampoo, one conditioner, one body wash, all readable and above a third full, over a non-slip tub floor.
cards.trigger: When you strip the guest bed after a visit, carry out whatever the guest left in the shower on the same trip to the laundry.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Spray the grout lines and the bottom band of the liner, then leave them to dwell while you finish elsewhere.
Wipe the sticky ring left under each bottle on the caddy or shelf.
Wipe the shower head and arm where scale has started to crust the spray holes.

art.subject: a guest bathroom shower with three bottles standing in a hanging caddy, a clean curtain liner with no pink film at its hem, a folded bath mat draped over the tub rim, evenly colored grout in every corner, a non-slip ridged tub floor, and one securely anchored grab bar fixed to the tiled wall, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: TOILET AREA STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: One reserve roll visible from the seat, a dry brush in a dry holder, a lined can, and no ring at the water line.
cards.trigger: Trash collection night is liner night in here, and the reserve roll gets checked while you are holding the bag.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the flush handle on every face, since it is the one thing every guest touches.
Lift the seat and wipe its underside and the rim it sits on, the part most often missed.
Rinse the brush holder so no liquid pools in its bottom before it goes back.

art.subject: a guest bathroom toilet area with one spare roll standing in a holder within easy seated reach, a dry brush resting in its holder, a small lined trash can, a clean bowl with no ring at the water line, and a dust-free floor behind the pedestal, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: GUEST LINEN ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Two complete bundles, bath towel plus hand towel plus washcloth in each, and the bath mat folded beneath.
cards.trigger: The guest's departure is the trigger: strip the bed and the bathroom together, wash them together, restock the shelf before you sit down.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the front lip of one shelf where hands grip to pull a towel stack out.
Run a hand along the back wall of the closet, checking for damp.
Refold one bundle so a hand's width of air sits above the finished stack.

art.subject: a linen closet shelf holding two matching complete towel bundles each with a bath towel, hand towel and washcloth folded together, a folded bath mat lying flat beneath them, a hand's width of clear air above the stack, and no thin gray towel sharing the shelf, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: THE UNANNOUNCED DROP-IN
cards.objective: A friend calls from the driveway, already parking, and the guest counter has to answer for itself with zero notice.
cards.held_if: The soap pump is full, a fresh hand towel hangs on the ring, and nothing personal is anywhere in sight.
cards.if_it_failed: If a stray toothbrush or a half-empty soap pump greeted them instead, the visit-confirmed walk-through did not happen. Draw GHA-002.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand towel hanging fresh on a guest bathroom counter ring moments before a doorbell rings
must_show: A friend calls from the driveway, already parking, and the guest counter has to answer for itself with zero notice.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE OVERNIGHT GUEST WHO FORGOT A TOOTHBRUSH
cards.objective: A guest arrives without a toothbrush and has to ask, or hopes the cabinet already has one.
cards.held_if: The guest supplies bin opens to a new toothbrush, a wrapped soap and four fresh travel toiletries, no rummaging required.
cards.if_it_failed: If the bin was empty or stuffed with old miniatures instead, the sort-and-restock pass slipped. Draw GHA-003.

cards.title: THE GUEST WHO SHOWERS AT ELEVEN AT NIGHT
cards.objective: A guest showers well after dark, in an unfamiliar tub, on a floor they cannot judge by feel alone.
cards.held_if: A non-slip mat grips the tub floor, one solidly anchored grab bar is exactly where a reaching hand finds it, and three full bottles are easy to read in dim light.
cards.if_it_failed: If they reached for a towel bar instead of a grab bar, or found the floor slick, the safety pass slipped. Draw GHA-006.

cards.held_if: The reserve roll stands in reach from the seat, in the same spot it always is.
cards.if_it_failed: If they had to get up and hunt for it, the roll never got remounted within seated reach. Draw GHA-008.

cards.title: TWO GUESTS ARRIVE INSTEAD OF ONE
cards.objective: A second guest turns up unannounced and the linen shelf has to produce a full second set on the spot.
cards.held_if: Two complete bundles already stand on the shelf up to the marked line, each one lift away.
cards.if_it_failed: If only one bundle was ready, or towels had to be gathered from three different stacks, the departure reset or the bundling pass slipped. Draw GHA-010.
